title: Kingdom of Kerma
description: A town around a great mud-brick temple becomes the capital of the first large state south of Egypt.

title: Piye conquers Egypt
description: The Kushite king marches north from Napata and makes the rulers of Egypt submit, founding its Twenty-fifth Dynasty.

title: Egyptians sack Napata
description: An army sent by Psamtik II raids deep into Kush, after which the kings rule from Meroë further south.

title: Royal burials move to Meroë
description: Kushite kings begin to be buried under pyramids at Meroë, a centre of iron-working with its own script.

title: War between Kush and Rome
description: After Kushites raid Aswan, the Roman prefect Petronius sacks Napata, and a treaty then fixes the frontier for three centuries.

title: Aksum invades Meroë
description: King Ezana of Aksum records a campaign on the Nile, by which time the Kushite kingdom has broken up.

title: Nobatia converts to Christianity
description: A mission sent by the empress Theodora converts the northern Nubian court, and the other Nubian kingdoms follow within a few decades.

title: Battle of Dongola and the Baqt
description: Makurian archers hold off an Arab army from Egypt, and the treaty that follows keeps peace between Christian Nubia and Egypt for centuries.

title: Throne hall of Dongola becomes a mosque
description: A Muslim king takes the throne of Makuria and converts its throne hall, a sign of the end of Christian Nubia.

title: Funj Sultanate founded
description: Amara Dunqas founds a kingdom on the Blue Nile that soon adopts Islam and rules central Sudan for three centuries.

title: Sultanate of Darfur founded
description: The Keira dynasty of the Fur founds a Muslim sultanate in the mountains of the west that lasts, with one break, until 1916.

title: Egyptian conquest
description: An army sent by Muhammad Ali of Egypt takes Sennar without a fight and ends the Funj Sultanate, and Khartoum is founded as the new capital.

title: Muhammad Ahmad declares himself the Mahdi
description: A religious teacher on the White Nile proclaims himself the awaited redeemer and calls for holy war against Egyptian rule.

title: Battle of Shaykan
description: The Mahdi's army destroys an Egyptian force of about 10,000 men under the British officer William Hicks.

title: Fall of Khartoum
description: After a siege of ten months the Mahdists take the city and kill General Charles Gordon, two days before a relief force arrives.

title: Battle of Omdurman
description: Kitchener's Anglo-Egyptian army, with machine guns and artillery, kills about 12,000 of the Khalifa's men and ends the Mahdist State.

title: Fashoda Incident
description: Kitchener confronts a French expedition under Marchand on the White Nile, and France backs down and leaves the Nile valley to Britain.

title: Anglo-Egyptian Condominium
description: Britain and Egypt agree to rule Sudan jointly, in practice under British governors, until 1956.

title: Darfur annexed
description: An Anglo-Egyptian force defeats Sultan Ali Dinar, who had sided with the Ottomans, and adds Darfur to Sudan.

title: Torit mutiny
description: Southern soldiers mutiny against their northern officers months before independence, the start of the first civil war.

title: Independence
description: Sudan becomes independent of Britain and Egypt as a parliamentary republic.

title: October Revolution
description: A general strike after police kill a student makes General Ibrahim Abboud hand power back to civilians.

title: Khartoum Resolution
description: After the Six-Day War, Arab leaders meeting in Khartoum declare no peace with Israel, no recognition and no negotiation.

title: Nimeiry takes power
description: Colonel Jaafar Nimeiry overthrows the civilian government and rules for sixteen years.

title: Addis Ababa Agreement
description: The government and southern rebels end the first civil war by giving the south its own regional government, which lasts eleven years.

title: Second civil war begins
description: Southern troops mutiny at Bor and John Garang forms the Sudan People's Liberation Army, starting a war that lasts 22 years and costs about two million lives.

title: Bashir takes power
description: Omar al-Bashir overthrows the elected government of Sadiq al-Mahdi with Islamist backing and rules for thirty years.

title: War in Darfur begins
description: Rebels attack government posts, and the army and Janjaweed militias answer by destroying villages, killing some hundreds of thousands and driving millions from their homes.

title: Comprehensive Peace Agreement
description: The government and the Sudan People's Liberation Movement end the second civil war and give the south a vote on independence after six years.

title: South Sudan becomes independent
description: After a referendum the south secedes, taking with it about a quarter of the country's land and most of its oil.

title: Bashir overthrown
description: After four months of street protests the army removes Omar al-Bashir, and in August it agrees to share power with civilians.
